Title: Turn a counsel email thread into an open-issues list
Subject: Friday Copilot Tip: Turn a long counsel email thread into an open-issues list
WhyItMatters: You get a who-owes-what-by-when list from a long lender/borrower counsel thread in minutes, instead of rebuilding it by hand before every call.
TipSteps: Open Copilot Chat (in new Outlook or Outlook on the web, select the Copilot button at the top; or go to m365.cloud.microsoft/chat) and make sure Work IQ is turned on | Type / and use the Emails tab to add the most recent messages in the thread | Paste the prompt below and send | Check each item against the cited emails before you circulate the list, and keep it marked draft until an attorney has reviewed it
TryPrompt: Using the emails I referenced, build an open-issues list for the [Borrower] / [Lender] [loan type] closing for [Property]. Table columns: # | Issue | Raised by (name and side) | Who owes the next action | What is owed | Due date (write 'none stated' if no date) | Status (open, agreed, closed) | Date of the latest email on it. Treat an issue as closed only if both sides confirmed it in writing. List items with no clear owner in a separate section. Do not guess dates or owners.
LearnLabel: Refer to specific files and more in Microsoft Copilot
VideoLabel: Catch Up on Long Email Threads Faster with Copilot
Notes: Needs Work IQ turned on in Copilot Chat so / can add emails.

Title: Abstract loan terms into a table in Word
Subject: Friday Copilot Tip: Abstract a loan agreement's key terms into a table
WhyItMatters: A first-pass term abstract with section references lets you check terms against the source instead of typing them from scratch.
TipSteps: Open the [term sheet or loan agreement] in Word, select the Copilot button, and choose Chat only so Copilot does not change the document | Paste the prompt below; for a long agreement, run it one article at a time | Use the citations in Copilot's response to jump to each source passage and confirm every number, date and party name | Copy the checked table into your abstract template and keep it marked draft until reviewed
TryPrompt: Do not edit this document. Create a table abstracting these terms from this [loan agreement / term sheet]: borrower, guarantor(s), lender, loan amount, interest rate (fixed or floating, index, spread, floor), default rate, maturity date and extension options, amortization and interest-only period, prepayment (lockout, yield maintenance or defeasance, open period), reserves (tax, insurance, replacement, other), financial covenants (DSCR, LTV, debt yield), cash management triggers, recourse carve-outs and guaranties, and transfer provisions. Columns: Term | Summary | Section reference | Exact quote. Write 'Not found' if a term is not in the document. Do not infer or fill gaps.
LearnLabel: Chat with Copilot about your Word document

Title: What Copilot can see: the confidentiality basics
Subject: Friday Copilot Tip: What Copilot can and cannot see in the firm's data
WhyItMatters: Knowing that Copilot works inside the firm's existing Microsoft 365 permissions and data protections helps you use it on client matters with confidence and spot oversharing early.
TipSteps: Copilot only surfaces firm content you already have at least view permission to, using the same permissions as SharePoint, OneDrive, Outlook and Teams | Your prompts and responses are covered by the firm's Microsoft 365 enterprise terms and are not used to train the foundation models | Copilot respects sensitivity labels and the firm's retention and audit settings; follow firm policy and any client outside counsel guidelines that limit AI use | If Copilot shows you something you should not see (for example, a walled-off matter), stop, do not use it, and tell IT so the file permissions can be fixed
TryPrompt: For [matter name or number], list the documents, emails and Teams chats you would draw on to answer questions about this matter, with each item's location and owner. Do not summarize their contents. Flag any item that appears to belong to a different client or matter.
LearnLabel: Data, Privacy, and Security for Microsoft Copilot
VideoLabel: Privacy, security, and compliance in Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat
Notes: Reviewer: confirm the firm's AI policy and any client outside counsel guidelines before sending.

Title: Closing call recap: decisions, owners, deadlines
Subject: Friday Copilot Tip: Get decisions and action items from a closing call
WhyItMatters: You leave a closing call with a reviewable list of decisions, owners and deadlines, and you can check what was agreed while the call is still running.
TipSteps: When you schedule the call, set Online meeting options > Copilot and other AI to During and after the meeting, and start transcription when the call begins (Copilot does not work in meetings hosted outside the firm) | During the call, select Copilot in the meeting controls to ask private questions, for example: What has [lender's counsel] agreed to so far? | After the call, open the meeting chat, go to the Recap tab, open Copilot and paste the prompt below | Select Open in Word to edit, then check the list against your own notes before you circulate it
TryPrompt: From the transcript and chat of this closing call, list: (1) decisions made, with who agreed; (2) action items in a table: Action | Owner (name and side) | Due date stated | Related document; (3) issues still open, with each side's position in one line; (4) anything someone said they would check or come back on. Mark anything ambiguous as 'confirm'. Do not add items that were not discussed.
LearnLabel: Catch up on meetings with Microsoft Copilot in Teams
VideoLabel: Catch up your way with Copilot in Teams
Notes: Copilot does not work in Teams meetings hosted outside the firm; works when a firm attorney hosts. Transcription must be on.

Title: Explain a dense loan clause in plain English
Subject: Friday Copilot Tip: Explain a prepayment clause to a client in plain English
WhyItMatters: Clients understand yield maintenance, cash management and recourse terms faster when you send a plain-English explanation and worked example you have checked against the clause.
TipSteps: Select the clause in Word, then select Copilot from the mini toolbar | Describe the rewrite you want (prompt below) | Choose Insert below to keep the original next to the new version, or Regenerate for another version; avoid Replace in the agreement itself | Move the checked explanation into your client email or memo, and make any drafting changes in the agreement yourself with Review > Track Changes on
TryPrompt: Rewrite this [prepayment / yield maintenance / cash management] clause in plain English for a [borrower client / lender relationship manager] who is not a lawyer. Keep every number, date, percentage and condition. Use short sentences and add a worked example using [assumed loan amount, rate and prepayment date]. Then, separately, suggest two alternative drafting options that would be more [borrower / lender] favorable, each with one line on the business effect. Do not change the meaning in the plain-English version. This will go to a client, so flag anything you are unsure about.
LearnLabel: Edit content and rewrite

Title: Prep for a client or counterparty call in Outlook
Subject: Friday Copilot Tip: Prep for a counterparty call from your Outlook calendar
WhyItMatters: Copilot pulls the recent emails, chats and shared documents tied to a meeting so you walk into the call knowing what is open on each side.
TipSteps: Open the call in your calendar in new Outlook for Windows or Outlook on the web | Review the Prepare for this meeting content at the top and select Show more, or select the Prepare for this meeting button to continue in chat | Paste the prompt below | Check anything you plan to rely on; Copilot only uses content you can access, and meetings with little related content get generic answers
TryPrompt: For my call with [counterparty or client] about the [Property] [loan type] closing, give me: (1) a five-bullet status of where the deal stands based on recent emails, chats and shared documents; (2) open items we are waiting on from them and items they are waiting on from us, with the date of the email or chat for each; (3) three questions to ask that move us toward a [target closing date] closing. Cite your sources.
LearnLabel: Prepare for your meeting with Copilot
Notes: IT: Microsoft 365 admin center > Search & Intelligence > Meeting Insights must be enabled.

Title: Verify every citation, number and fact
Subject: Friday Copilot Tip: Verify citations and facts (ABA Formal Opinion 512)
WhyItMatters: ABA Formal Opinion 512 (July 2024) says lawyers must review generative AI output for accuracy, including citations to authority, so a quick verification list protects you and the client.
TipSteps: Never use Copilot as a source of case law, statutes or citations; pull and read each authority in Westlaw or Lexis | Ground Copilot in the document itself: reference the file with / and say Use this file only | Open the citations Copilot provides and read the cited passage; ask Confirm the publish date and show the exact section when it relies on a document | Use the prompt below to build a checklist, then tick off each item against the source documents yourself
TryPrompt: Use this file only: /[draft memo, closing letter or opinion]. List every factual statement, dollar amount, date, percentage, party name, section cross-reference and legal citation in a table: Item | Where it appears (section or paragraph) | What it should be checked against ([loan agreement], [title commitment], [survey], Westlaw or Lexis). Do not correct anything, do not add citations, and do not say whether any authority is valid.
LearnLabel: What information does Copilot use to answer my prompt?
VideoLabel: How grounding works in Microsoft 365 Copilot
Notes: ABA Formal Opinion 512 (July 29, 2024). If linking it, open the americanbar.org page in a browser first (it blocks automated checks).

Title: Check a rent roll with Copilot in Excel
Subject: Friday Copilot Tip: Check a rent roll for totals and outliers in Excel
WhyItMatters: You can tie out occupancy and rent totals and spot anomalies in a borrower's rent roll before they become a diligence or underwriting question.
TipSteps: Open the rent roll and make sure the data is a clean table: one header row, no merged cells or subtotal rows | Select the Copilot icon in the lower-right corner; choose Chat only to analyze without changes, or Plan to review Copilot's approach before it edits | Paste the prompt below, then select any formula cell and ask: Explain the formula in the selected cell | Tie the totals back to the certified rent roll and the lender's underwriting before you rely on them
TryPrompt: This sheet is the rent roll for [Property] dated [date]. Using the table in [sheet or range]: (1) total units, occupied and vacant units, and physical occupancy %; (2) total monthly in-place rent and average rent by unit type; (3) leases expiring in the next [12] months; (4) outliers: rents more than [20]% above or below the average for that unit type, $0 rents, duplicate unit numbers, and move-in dates after the rent roll date. Show the results in a new sheet with the formulas used. Do not change the source data.
LearnLabel: Get data insights with Copilot in Excel

Title: Check defined terms and cross-references in Word
Subject: Friday Copilot Tip: Catch undefined terms and broken cross-references
WhyItMatters: A defined-term and cross-reference sweep gives you a punch list of drafting errors before a loan document goes to the other side.
TipSteps: Open the draft in Word, select the Copilot button, and choose Chat only so nothing in the document changes | Paste the prompt below; for a long agreement, run it one article at a time because Copilot can give less attention to the middle of long files | Treat the output as a to-do list, not a sign-off; make fixes yourself with Track Changes on and keep proofreading as usual
TryPrompt: Chat only, do not edit. Review [Article X / Sections X to Y] of this [loan agreement] against the definitions in [Section 1.1 or the definitions exhibit]. List in a table: (1) capitalized terms used but not defined; (2) terms defined more than once or defined inconsistently; (3) defined terms that are never used; (4) cross-references to sections, exhibits or schedules that do not exist or appear to point to the wrong provision. Columns: Issue | Term or reference | Where it appears | Exact text. If you are not sure, write 'check'.
LearnLabel: Welcome to Copilot in Word

Title: Draft a client status update from the matter file
Subject: Friday Copilot Tip: Draft a client status update from recent emails and docs
WhyItMatters: Copilot pulls recent emails, chats and the latest checklist into a first draft, so your weekly client update takes minutes to check rather than an hour to write.
TipSteps: In new Outlook or Outlook on the web, select the Copilot button at the top of Outlook | Paste the prompt below; it draws on your inbox, chats and the files you name | Copy the draft into a new message and edit it in your own voice | Verify every date, dollar amount and status against the documents before you send; this goes to the client
TryPrompt: Summarize my emails and Teams chats from the last [two weeks] about the [Property] / [Borrower] [loan type] financing, together with /[latest issues list] and /[latest closing checklist]. Draft a status email to [client contact] covering: where we are, what was completed since [date], open items (who owes what, by when), what we need from the client, and the target closing date. Professional and concise, no internal commentary. Flag any item where the sources conflict.
LearnLabel: Chat with Copilot in Outlook

Title: Turn rough notes into time-entry narratives
Subject: Friday Copilot Tip: Turn rough daily notes into clean time-entry narratives
WhyItMatters: Clear, task-specific narratives reduce billing write-downs and client questions, while the time itself still comes from your own records.
TipSteps: Open Copilot Chat and paste your rough notes for the day, with the matter number and the actual time for each task from your own records | Give a clear goal, context, source and expectations in one prompt (example below), including the client's billing guidelines | Ask Copilot to flag anything vague instead of filling gaps | Check each entry against your time records before you submit; under ABA Formal Opinion 512 hourly billing must reflect actual time spent
TryPrompt: Turn my notes below into time-entry narratives for matter [matter number]. Follow [client] billing guidelines: one entry per task, no block billing, start each entry with an action verb (review, draft, revise, confer), name the document or counterparty, and keep each entry under [40] words. Use only what is in my notes and keep my time for each task exactly as written. Do not add tasks or time. List anything unclear as a question for me. Notes: [paste notes]
LearnLabel: Get started writing prompts in Microsoft Copilot

Title: Summarize the business changes between two drafts
Subject: Friday Copilot Tip: Summarize the business changes between two loan drafts
WhyItMatters: Clients and deal teams want to know what moved commercially, not every comma, and a Copilot summary checked against Word's blackline gets you there faster.
TipSteps: For the exact blackline, keep using Word: Review > Compare > Compare Documents | For a business-level summary, in OneDrive on the web select both drafts (up to 5 files), then More actions (...) > Copilot > Compare files | In the Copilot panel, continue the chat with the prompt below | Check every point against the blackline before it goes to the client
TryPrompt: Compare these drafts of the [loan agreement / term sheet]: [Draft 1, date] and [Draft 2, date]. Summarize business changes only; ignore formatting, numbering and typo fixes. Table: Provision | Draft 1 | Draft 2 | Business effect for [Borrower / Lender] | Section. Cover economics (amount, rate, fees, prepayment), reserves, covenants, recourse and guaranties, transfers, defaults and closing conditions. Mark anything you are unsure about as 'confirm against blackline'.
LearnLabel: Compare your files with Copilot in OneDrive
Notes: Copilot summary is for business changes only; the Word blackline (Review > Compare) remains the record.

Title: Build a closing checklist from the commitment letter
Subject: Friday Copilot Tip: Build a closing checklist from the commitment letter
WhyItMatters: Every closing condition in the commitment or term sheet lands on the checklist with a source reference, which cuts the risk of a missed deliverable.
TipSteps: Open the firm's checklist template in Word (Copilot can keep its format and structure) or a blank document | Open Copilot, describe the checklist you need, then type / and choose the commitment letter or term sheet | Select Generate, then keep, regenerate or refine the draft with a follow-up prompt | Compare the result against the firm's standard checklist and the lender's closing requirements before you circulate it
TryPrompt: Using /[commitment letter or term sheet], create a closing checklist for the [Fannie Mae / Freddie Mac / CMBS / bridge] loan to [Borrower] secured by [Property]. Table columns: # | Document or deliverable | Responsible party (lender counsel, borrower counsel, borrower, title, surveyor, other) | Source section | Status | Notes. Group by: loan documents; organizational and authority documents; title and survey; third-party reports; insurance; reserves and escrows; opinions; closing and funding. Then add a separate diligence request list for the borrower. Include only items supported by the source; mark anything you add from general practice as '[standard, confirm]'.
LearnLabel: Draft and add content with Copilot in Word

Title: Find the latest draft or a precedent with Search
Subject: Friday Copilot Tip: Find the latest draft or a prior precedent with Search
WhyItMatters: Finding the current draft and a usable precedent quickly avoids marking up a stale version or redrafting a provision the firm has already negotiated.
TipSteps: In the Microsoft Copilot app (Microsoft365.com), select Search from the navigation pane and search by matter or document name | Use filters to narrow to files, then select + New to filter by Location, Shared by or Owned by | To go further, open Copilot Chat and paste the prompt below | Confirm the version in the file's version history or your document management system before you rely on it; Copilot only sees Microsoft 365 content you can access
TryPrompt: Find files I have access to related to [matter name or number] that look like versions of the [loan agreement / guaranty / closing checklist]. List file name, location, last modified date and by whom, newest first, and say which appears to be the current draft and why. Then list up to five prior [loan type] [document type] files I can access that could serve as precedent, with location. Do not summarize the contents.
LearnLabel: Get started with Search in the Microsoft Copilot app
Notes: Copilot only sees Microsoft 365 content. A separate DMS (iManage, NetDocuments) is invisible unless IT has connected it.

Title: Turn a memo into a client or CLE deck
Subject: Friday Copilot Tip: Turn a Word memo into a client or CLE presentation
WhyItMatters: Starting from your own memo gives you a structured first draft of a client briefing or CLE deck, so your time goes into the content rather than the slides.
TipSteps: Start a new presentation from the firm's PowerPoint template, then open Copilot from the icon at the bottom-right and choose the firm's Brand Kit if asked | Type or select Create presentation from file and pick your Word memo by searching your files or pasting its link | Paste the prompt below and answer Copilot's clarifying questions | Check every slide and speaker note against the memo; verify any citation before a CLE or client sees it
TryPrompt: Use the memo only. Create a [10 to 12] slide presentation for [audience: client deal team / CLE attendees] on [topic, for example key terms in agency multifamily loan documents]. One idea per slide, plain language, no more than five bullets per slide, speaker notes for each slide, and a final slide of open questions. Do not add facts, statistics or legal citations that are not in the memo.
LearnLabel: Create a new presentation with Copilot in PowerPoint
VideoLabel: How Copilot can create and edit your PowerPoint presentation for you

Title: Run a shared closing issues list in Copilot Pages
Subject: Friday Copilot Tip: Run the deal team's issues list in a shared Copilot Page
WhyItMatters: One live, editable issues list that the deal team and Copilot both update replaces versions of the same checklist circulating by email.
TipSteps: In Copilot Chat, ask for the list using the prompt below and reference the source files with / | Under the response, select the ellipses (...) and then Edit in Pages to open it as a page | Edit the page directly or ask Copilot to update it as items close | Select Share > Copy link to send it to the internal deal team; they see only the page, not your chat
TryPrompt: Create a page called '[Property] [loan type] closing issues'. Using /[latest issues list] and /[closing checklist], build a table: # | Item | Owner (firm or side) | Due | Status | Last update. Add a 'Recently closed' section at the bottom. Keep it plain and easy to scan. Later updates: 'Mark items [3] and [7] closed as of [date] and move them to Recently closed.'
LearnLabel: Get started with Microsoft Copilot Pages

Title: Build a team prompt library for recurring tasks
Subject: Friday Copilot Tip: Share your best deal prompts with your practice group
WhyItMatters: A shared set of tested prompts for recurring closing tasks gives everyone on the team consistent, firm-quality results without starting from scratch.
TipSteps: Run a prompt that works well, hover over it and select Save prompt; give it a clear name such as 'Post-closing obligations list' | Open the Copilot Prompt Gallery in Copilot Chat, Teams or Outlook and go to the Your prompts tab | Hover over the prompt, select Share prompt, then Share to team and pick your practice group's team | Colleagues find it in the Prompts app under Team prompts; remove prompts that go stale
TryPrompt: Using /[closing binder index] and /[final closing statement], list every post-closing obligation for the [Property] [loan type] loan: recording of security instruments, final title policy, original note delivery, reserve or escrow funding, insurance certificates, entity filings and any lender post-closing conditions. Table: Obligation | Responsible party | Due date or trigger | Source document and section. Mark anything not stated in the documents as 'confirm'.
LearnLabel: Sharing prompts with a Team
VideoLabel: Create and share prompts in your organization

Title: Set up a deal notebook and ask across documents
Subject: Friday Copilot Tip: Put a deal's documents in one Notebook and ask across them
WhyItMatters: A Notebook keeps Copilot's answers scoped to the deal documents you choose, so you can check terms across the term sheet, commitment and drafts in one place.
TipSteps: In the Microsoft Copilot app (m365.cloud.microsoft), select Notebooks > All notebooks > New notebook and name it for the deal | Under Add content to References, add the term sheet, commitment, current drafts, third-party reports and the issues list, then select Create | Set instructions (More options (...) > Instructions), for example: cite the document and section for every answer | Before you select Share, check the invitee list; sharing a notebook also invites recipients to the linked files
TryPrompt: Using only the references in this notebook, compare the [loan amount, interest rate, maturity, prepayment terms, reserves and guaranty] as stated in the [term sheet], [commitment letter] and current draft [loan agreement]. Show a table with one row per term, one column per document with section references, and a flag where they differ. Do not resolve differences; list them for attorney review.
LearnLabel: Get started with Microsoft Copilot Notebooks
Notes: Sharing a notebook invites recipients to every linked file. Check ethical walls before sharing.

Title: Use Researcher for market background, not law
Subject: Friday Copilot Tip: Use Researcher for market background (never for case law)
WhyItMatters: Researcher builds a cited background report on a market or lending program before a pitch or client meeting, leaving legal research to Westlaw and Lexis.
TipSteps: In the Microsoft Copilot app, select Researcher under Agents | Paste the prompt below and say whether to use the web, your work files, or both | Answer Researcher's clarifying questions, or say Go ahead | Open the cited sources and confirm dates and figures; do not use the report for legal authority or send it to a client without review
TryPrompt: Research current conditions for [Fannie Mae / Freddie Mac multifamily / CMBS / bridge] lending in [market or MSA] over the last [12] months: lending volumes, typical loan terms, the interest rate environment, and publicly announced program or guide changes. Use public web sources only, not my work files. Cite every source with its publication date and flag anything older than [6] months. Do not provide legal analysis or case law.
LearnLabel: Get started with Researcher in Microsoft Copilot

Title: Build a closing checklist agent from firm templates
Subject: Friday Copilot Tip: Build an agent grounded in the firm's checklist templates
WhyItMatters: An agent that answers only from the firm's approved checklists and templates gives the whole team consistent starting points for every closing.
TipSteps: In the Microsoft Copilot app, under Agents select New agent, then Skip to configure | Name the agent, paste the instructions below, and under Knowledge add the SharePoint folder that holds the firm's approved checklists and templates | Turn on Only use specified sources and test the agent on the Try it tab | Select Create, then share it only with your practice group and make sure they have access to the source folder
TryPrompt: You are the [practice group] closing checklist assistant. Use only the firm checklists and templates in your knowledge sources. When asked for a checklist for a [agency / CMBS / bridge / balance-sheet] closing, start from the matching firm template, list each item with the responsible party (lender counsel, borrower counsel, borrower, title, other) and timing, and name the template file you used. If no template matches, say so. Never invent requirements or cite law. Remind users to confirm against the commitment letter and the lender's closing instructions.
LearnLabel: Build agents in Agent Builder
Notes: May require admin to allow Agent Builder / agent sharing. Share only with the practice group.
